overview.mechanism: A vitamin D precursor converted to 25-hydroxyvitamin D and subsequently to active metabolites; it is distinct from calcitriol and alfacalcidol.
uses: Correction of vitamin D deficiency; CKD mineral and bone disorder requires assessment beyond the vitamin D concentration alone.

paragraphs.text: A randomized trial in 44 nondialysis patients with CKD G3–G5 found greater on-treatment 25-hydroxyvitamin D increases with cholecalciferol than ergocalciferol. PTH and active-vitamin-D changes were not significantly different, and levels declined after treatment stopped.

Biochemical repletion does not establish reduced fractures, cardiovascular events or kidney failure. A nutritional vitamin D preparation should not be substituted for an active analogue solely because both are called vitamin D.

sources.citation: Cholecalciferol v. ergocalciferol for 25-hydroxyvitamin D repletion in chronic kidney disease: a randomised clinical trial. PubMed PMID: 28065190.

revision_log.change: Source-linked descriptive overview and clinical evidence; no new unsupported dose recommendation or inferred dialysis schedule.
